scope: D041-D060 20 original questions and 80 A–D choices
approval_policy: Exact law/official agency source and every keyed/incorrect choice reviewed by author; no external blind reviewer required by owner
exam_day_recheck_policy: Reverify FDA product status, DEA/MA effective dates, and policy changes at actual exam date; especially FDA database and DPH circular.

items.law: FDA Orange Book Preface §1.7; Levothyroxine Sodium multi-code RLD

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. A shared AB1 is sufficient to establish FDA therapeutic equivalence for products under the same heading, with matching equivalent product details.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA Orange Book Preface §1.7; Levothyroxine Sodium multi-code RLD

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. The FDA preface explicitly discusses a product with multiple AB codes; one common code establishes a TE relationship to the multi-coded product.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA Orange Book Preface §1.7; Levothyroxine Sodium multi-code RLD

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. Different numbered codes alone do not establish equivalence directly between single-coded P and single-coded Q.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA Orange Book Preface §1.7; Levothyroxine Sodium multi-code RLD

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. The reference product may share more than one AB code; matching AB2 supports this relationship.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA Orange Book Preface §1.7; Levothyroxine Sodium multi-code RLD

items.substantive_novelty_difference: The multi-coded real Unithroid reference has TE links to two differently single-coded products; C118 only tests a single-coded reference.
items.date_or_scope_note: The generic P/Q products in the scenario are explicitly hypothetical, not claimed actual FDA-approved listings.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. Authorized generics are marketed under the original approved NDA rather than a newly approved ANDA.
Correct. 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2) requires authorized generic marketing details in the annual report; the FDA publishes the list.
Incorrect. Authorized generic annual reporting does not depend on a medication error.
Incorrect. The responsible annual-reporting party is the NDA holder.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: 21 CFR 314.81 NDA holder authorized-generic annual report, not permissible pharmacy substitution.
items.date_or_scope_note: Current official provisions were compared to the exact actor, setting, condition and alternate choices; recheck if law changes.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. The FDA Purple Book lists product 001 with 1,000 units/10 mL, multidose vial, license type 351(k) Interchangeable.
Incorrect. The record specifies subcutaneous injection, autoinjector, and interchangeable status.
Correct. The FDA entry explicitly lists the 300 units/3 mL autoinjector as product 002.
Incorrect. The listed reference product is specifically Lantus, not all basal insulins.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Exact FDA BLA product numbers, dose presentations and license status, not simply biosimilar vs interchangeable.
items.date_or_scope_note: FDA BLA product presentations are verified as of Nov 18 2026; may evolve.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The prohibition may be individual and patient-specific under §12EE(c).
Incorrect. EHR communication applies after a lawful substitution and cannot override an explicit written prohibition.
Incorrect. A request alone does not remove an operative patient-specific written no-substitution instruction.
Correct. M.G.L. c.112 §12EE(c) bars substitution if the prescriber instructs otherwise in writing for that patient.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Prescriber-written patient-specific prohibition actually reverses otherwise permissible biologic interchange.
items.date_or_scope_note: Current official provisions were compared to the exact actor, setting, condition and alternate choices; recheck if law changes.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. 21 CFR 201.17 expressly permits the date on individual cartons of single-dose containers.
Incorrect. A computer record does not substitute for federally required manufacturer/repackager labeling.
Incorrect. Repackaging does not erase the expiration-date labeling requirement.
Incorrect. The regulation provides a specific individual-carton exception.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Single-dose immediate container expiry placement exception, not pharmacy repackaging drug samples.
items.date_or_scope_note: Current official provisions were compared to the exact actor, setting, condition and alternate choices; recheck if law changes.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. A pharmacy prescription label does not replace a required FDA Medication Guide.
Correct. 21 CFR 208.24(e) requires providing the guide when a covered product is dispensed, barring an applicable exception.
Correct. FDA patient-labeling resources expressly describe patient-requested electronic delivery.
Incorrect. FDA explains Medication Guides can be labeling requirements without a REMS.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Patient-requested electronic Medication Guide delivery, not general requirement or prescriber exemption.
items.date_or_scope_note: Electronic MG upon patient request is described on FDA official Patient Labeling Resources; normal default remains paper.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. FDA does not waive PPIs solely because a nurse administers the medication.
Incorrect. Section 310.501(b)(2) provides an institutional alternative to providing a new insert with every unit dose.
Correct. The regulation expressly allows PPIs for oral contraceptives in acute-care hospitals and long-term-care facilities before the first dose and every 30 days while therapy continues.
Incorrect. The institutional exception requires repeat provision every 30 days while treatment continues.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: LTCF / acute care oral contraceptive PPI before first dose and every 30 days, not ordinary outpatient each-fill requirement.
items.date_or_scope_note: Institutional alternative is specifically acute-care hospitals or LTCF, not every retail prescription.

items.law: FDA July 2020 Unit-Dose Repackaging Guidance; 21 CFR 211.137/211.166

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The FDA policy compares six months with 25% of remaining time, not 50%.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA July 2020 Unit-Dose Repackaging Guidance; 21 CFR 211.137/211.166

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The original container's stability evidence does not automatically transfer to a different unit-dose package.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA July 2020 Unit-Dose Repackaging Guidance; 21 CFR 211.137/211.166

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. FDA's ordinary guideline also compares 25% of remaining shelf life; 25% of sixteen months is four months.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA July 2020 Unit-Dose Repackaging Guidance; 21 CFR 211.137/211.166

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. Twenty-five percent of 16 months is four months, which is shorter than six; this is FDA enforcement-discretion guidance for commercial firms, not a general legal pharmacy BUD.
correct_choice_rationales.source_primary: FDA July 2020 Unit-Dose Repackaging Guidance; 21 CFR 211.137/211.166

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Commercial FDA-registered repackaging firm nonbinding 6mo/25%-remaining FDA policy, not pharmacy compounding BUD.
items.date_or_scope_note: FDA 2020 guidance is NONBINDING and applies to commercial FDA-registered repackagers; 16-month remaining gives four months under shorter-of-6-months-or-25%-remaining conditions.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. Correct eligibility: the return occurs within 30 days of discontinuation and at least 90 days before expiration.
Incorrect. The regulation requires return at least 90 days before the earliest label expiration.
Incorrect. The return is beyond the 30-day deadline after discontinuation.
Correct. Both the 30-day discontinuation deadline and 90-day-before-expiration requirement are satisfied.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: MassHealth 130 CMR 456.621 nursing unit-dose return-for-credit 30-day and 90-day requirements, not pharmacy never-dispensed return-to-stock.
items.date_or_scope_note: The 30-day and at-least-90-days-before-expiry rules concern a MassHealth credit process, NOT routine re-dispensing of a previously dispensed drug.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The current text of 406.446 deals with drug review and counseling, not the old return provision.
Correct. The current MassHealth Nursing Facility Manual separately governs returns of unused specified unit-dose drugs.
Incorrect. CDTM protocol eligibility does not govern the nursing facility unit-dose return program.
Incorrect. Medication Guide rules are a different document-delivery requirement.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Current 130 CMR 406.446 prospective DUR vs 456.621 nursing unit-dose returns; old regulatory cross-reference superseded.
items.date_or_scope_note: Archived Pharmacy Manual Appendix D still points to older 406.446; 2026 PHM-65 revised 406.446 to DUR/counseling, and current nursing-facility 456.621 governs facility return.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The FDA definition of a recall concerns marketed violative product; the lot never left the firm's direct control.
Correct. Section 7.3(k) defines stock recovery for unreleased product still directly controlled by the firm.
Incorrect. Market withdrawal applies to distributed product in the particular minor/no-violation circumstances.
Incorrect. No pharmacy dispensed or transferred product in the scenario.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: FDA stock recovery for never-marketed manufacturer-controlled batch vs recall of distributed drug.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. Section 1317.15(c) requires secure storage or prompt authorized handling of controlled substances acquired by a reverse distributor.
Incorrect. A registrant's accounting does not waive the reverse distributor's 30-day destruction duty for destruction stock.
Correct. 21 CFR 1317.15(d) sets a 30-calendar-day deadline from the reverse distributor's receipt.
Incorrect. The regulation requires the authorized registered location and controlled custody, not unregistered diversion.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Reverse distributor's *own* secure storage and 30-calendar-day destruction clock, not a pharmacy's registered stock-transfer procedure.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. The 2025 Board policy §IV(G) requires pharmacy personnel administering vaccines to report vaccination information to MIIS.
Correct. CDC encourages voluntary reporting of clinically significant events regardless of proof that the vaccine caused them.
Incorrect. VAERS mandatory healthcare-provider reporting covers enumerated reportable events and manufacturer-listed contraindications, not every mild event.
Incorrect. MIIS immunization registry reporting is different from adverse-event reporting through VAERS.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: State MIIS administration record vs federal VAERS adverse-event categories; a mild postvaccination sore arm does not waive MIIS.
items.date_or_scope_note: A routine mild soreness is not the same as mandatory federal VAERS table event; state MIIS reporting is a separate obligation.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. VAERS applies to vaccination reports; naltrexone administration is not vaccination.
Incorrect. DPH guidance calls for appropriate communication of reactions, not proof of pharmacologic causation first.
Incorrect. The DPH circular establishes a 24-hour communication recommendation for non-serious reactions.
Correct. DCP 26-03-124 directs adverse reactions to be communicated within 24 hours, with event recording.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Nonvaccine injection nonserious reaction prescriber communication 24h, not pharmacy-compounded adverse-event Board reporting.
items.date_or_scope_note: DPH circular says nonserious AE *should* be reported to prescriber within 24h; this is guidance, NOT an unconditional statutory deadline.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. The March 2026 circular adds testosterone for gender-affirming care; single-dose IM route and adult eligibility are met.
Incorrect. Massachusetts DPH recognizes listed non-vaccine pharmacist administration pathways.
Incorrect. The circular establishes 18 years or older, not 21.
Incorrect. Patient administration under a valid prescription is distinct from ordering pharmacy Schedule II inventory.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Testosterone in gender-affirming care under new 2026 DPH list, rather than cabotegravir HIV PrEP nonvaccine injection.
items.date_or_scope_note: Current official provisions were compared to the exact actor, setting, condition and alternate choices; recheck if law changes.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The severity triggers immediate reporting rather than ordinary non-serious 24-hour communication.
Correct. DCP 26-03-124 requires immediate prescriber communication for life-threatening outcomes or ED treatment/monitoring.
Correct. DCP 26-03-124 states serious adverse drug events and events from dispensing errors remain reportable to the Board as applicable.

Correct. The DPH circular directs reporting to the Board in accordance with Board regulations. Section 20.02 has specific triggers, such as improper dispensing with serious injury/death or serious events involving drugs manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy; an ordinary injection reaction is not categorically reportable to the Board.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Post-injection life-threatening reaction requires immediate prescriber communication; independent Board reporting only if narrow 247 CMR20.02 triggers apply.
items.date_or_scope_note: Do not overstate all nonvaccine injection reactions as Board-mandatory; only if 247 CMR 20.02 or another regulation's precise trigger applies.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. DEA's 2026 revision removed that legacy application-signer pathway for POA execution.
Incorrect. The POA is granted on behalf of the corporate registrant; the problem is the grantor's actual corporate authority.
Correct. Section 1305.05(d)(1) prescribes the eligible grantor; being an HR application submitter alone does not qualify.
Incorrect. The federal POA rule requires two witnesses, not three.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: 2026 corporate POA grantor cannot be mere DEA-application signer, not revocation of already executed POA.
items.date_or_scope_note: 91 FR 13499 amended who can execute POA; older DEA application-signer text superseded in March 2026.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. The federal provision permits electronic signatures by any or all of the persons required to sign.
Correct. 21 CFR 1305.05(f) explicitly permits electronic execution by any or all required POA signers, including witnesses.
Incorrect. A compliant executed POA is retained with order records; individual DEA preapproval is not a requirement of §1305.05(f).
Incorrect. DEA recognizes electronically signed POAs separately from an individual CSOS signing certificate.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: POA executed by compliant electronic signatures of grantor, grantee and witnesses under §1305.05(f), rather than 2026 revocation authority.
items.date_or_scope_note: The electronic-signature permission predates 2026 update and remains in 1305.05(f); witness requirement still applies.

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Correct. The 2026 rule permits corporate officers of the registrant to sign Form 222 directly.
Incorrect. A professional or facility job title alone is not federal Form 222 signature authority.
Incorrect. Employment does not create an individual POA or corporate officer status.
Correct. Section 1305.12(d) also permits an individual with a lawful POA to sign for the registrant.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Corporate officer direct DEA Form222 signing vs MOR without POA; CSOS individual certificate permissions are a different task.
items.date_or_scope_note: Direct corporate-officer signing authorization as revised §1305.12(d).

correct_choice_rationales.explanation: Incorrect. Federal regulations require retaining the POA with order files, not resubmitting it for each order.
Incorrect. An inspector can require the executed written/electronic POA and its documented validity.
Incorrect. The POA retention period follows the signed orders and is not exhausted by first use.
Correct. Section 1305.05(a) directly requires retention for the same period as orders bearing the attorney's signature and inspection availability.

items.substantive_novelty_difference: Physical/electronic POA instrument must be retained with orders/inspectable, not mere authority to revoke.
